$comment: Template-owned: template-actors (decision 0001). One manifest per actor: .github/actors/<slug>.yml. scripts/actors.py check validates every manifest against this, then the rules a schema can't say (one App per role, shared Apps agree, no secret values).
title: Actor manifest
description: An identity this repository's automation acts as. The manifest is the source of truth; vault actor notes are generated from it (scripts/actors.py note). Never a key or token: only the pass path of a key.

name.description: The actor's display name, Title Case (Tagwarden, Night Scribe).

emoji.description: The emoji its vault note's name starts with.

description.description: One line: what it does in the real automation.

theme.description: The owner's theme: the style block its avatar takes.

status.description: planned -> created (the App exists) -> installed (on its repos) -> active (doing its job) -> retired, superseded (wholly replaced, by superseded_by) or deleted (the App or job is gone).

identity.description: What it acts as. Only github-app actors have an App, ids, a key, roles and a fallback.

runs_as.description: Every identity but github-app: whose rights it uses (GITHUB_TOKEN, dependabot[bot], a deploy key and a gh login).

app.description: github-app only: the App's slug. One App may serve several actors (Chronicler runs on Tagwarden's): give each the same app, app_id, client_id and key.

app_id.description: github-app only: the App ID from its settings page. Public, not a secret.

client_id.description: github-app only: the Client ID from its settings page. Public, not a secret. actors-setup.py sets it as <ROLE>_APP_CLIENT_ID.

key.description: github-app only: the pass path of the App's private key (actors/<slug>/private-key). Never the key. actors-setup.py pipes it into <ROLE>_APP_PRIVATE_KEY.

permissions.description: What it can do, least needed: the App's or token's permissions as scope: level. A local actor lists what it does with the rights it runs as.

acts_on.description: Where it is installed or acts, as GitHub owner/name.

trigger.description: What starts it: this repository's workflow files and their events, a cron schedule, or a local command.

schedule.description: Five-field cron, UTC for workflows, local time for a local actor.

roles.description: github-app only: the roles it fills, which name its secrets (decision 0001, question 2): update -> UPDATE_APP_*, release -> RELEASE_APP_*, brain-pull -> BRAIN_PULL_APP_*.

merge_policy.description: Who merges its PRs. never: a person. auto-on-ci: auto-merge, once the required checks pass. auto-after-codeowner: auto-merge, once the required checks pass and a code owner approves (the ruleset's required review holds it).

merge_method.description: How an auto-merged PR merges. squash unless its branch lives on (a live branch merges).

fallback.description: github-app only: without the App's variable, fail or skip (required), or use github.token (github-token) and accept that CI won't run on its PRs and a workflow change becomes an issue.

labels.description: The labels its PRs carry, created idempotently (actors.py labels, actors-labels.yml).

branch_prefix.description: Every branch its PRs come from starts with this (release-please--, chore/template-update, auto/nightly). Required unless merge_policy is never.

avatar.description: The avatar: a PNG (actors-avatar.py: 1024x1024, 256 colours, under 1 MB, legible at 20 to 64 px) and the prompt it was made from, without the theme's style block.

superseded_by.description: Wholly replaced: the successor's slug, with status superseded. Partly replaced: a list of {actor, scope}, the part each successor took over, while this one keeps the rest.
